evidence_layer: synthetic memory oracle: the original ARM bytes of THREE bodies (0x1ab654 CRoom::AddInstance, 0x1c5d18 CLayerManager::AddInstance, 0x1c5a38 CLayerManager::AddInstanceToLayer) executed over the image's own .bss cells, with F1's bl landing in F2/F3's original bytes and every unrecovered callee stubbed identically on both arms; NOT device execution

heap_model.note: the fill byte is asserted, not incidental: bytes no body writes must still compare equal across the two arms

covered: F1: count increment before the empty-chain branch; walk on the SNAPSHOT +0x184; bls (<=, unordered) stop; tail append via room+0x80; head/middle splice; id-hash append at the bucket TAIL with no duplicate check; the bl into F2; the b into CollisionInsert and the resulting return value

F2: all four gates in machine order (Zeus byte polarity, room, instance, +0x174); the cmn #1 layer-id sentinel vs a real id 0; GetLayerFromID hit/miss; the vcvt.s32.f32 truncation on 2.9 / -2.9 / 1e10 / -1e10 / NaN / -0.9; the hard-coded TRUE third argument; level 2 hit suppresses level 3; AddDynamicLayer; the tail jump into F3

F3: the three gates; hash + 31-bit clear + mask from the room; the 12 B bucket stride; empty bucket, first-bucket hash match, probe advance, probe hash match, probe insert-here, probe into an empty bucket; value NULL; the owned/unowned split; the error vtable call and its "writes nothing" contract; the pool grow loop (one and two elements), the capacity doubling, the capacity <= 0 double-only path, the free-list pop with prev 0 / prev != 0 / next 0; the uid counter read-then-increment; the three instance field writes; both tails (AddElementToLayer with the deactivated byte, UpdateInstanceActivation)
not_covered: the semantics of every stubbed callee: a green run says the chain passes the right ARGUMENTS to them and passes their r0 through, nothing more
the real CHashMapCalculateHash: the harness uses a documented model (key*2654435761), so only the probe STATE MACHINE is graded, not the original hash

F3's 0x1c5ac0 `tst r2,r4 ; bpl` early-out: it can only fall through when the table mask has bit 31 set, which needs a 0x80000000-entry table.  The instruction is translated and documented, but no case takes that edge.  Same for the dead guards at 0x1c5c64 (idx == -1) and 0x1c5c74 (bucket == -4)

F3's 0x1c5b10 branch on Alloc returning NULL: taken only when the allocator fails, and the fall-through writes through a NULL pointer, so staging it measures a fault, not behaviour. The Alloc stub never returns NULL
F1 does not check room == NULL (it dereferences r0 at 0x1ab65c); a NULL-room case would abort both arms inside the first body and prove nothing, so it is not staged
the class identity of the host object whose vtable+0xc is called on the error path (card open) and what the real CollisionInsert returns (the body reads its r0)
device behaviour: this is a synthetic-memory oracle over the original bytes, not execution on a phone
observability: every case compares the returned word, every word of every staged region (11 regions, pointers normalised to region / alloc tokens) and every allocated block, so a store the translation forgot and a store it invented both show up

the call log records each stub call in order with the arguments the body passed: the layer id, the truncated depth, the bool, the deactivated byte and the element pointer are read out of the log, not out of the input
the three tails return magic constants, so "does this body return its tail callee's r0" is graded, not assumed

staging_geometry.shared: one write program interpreted by both arms; only the region bases differ (the judge arm uses the image's own .bss cells for H/Z/G/P, the claim arm its own globals)

findings: CARD DRIFT: the F3 error host is GOT slot 0x3ed71c -> 0x3eb70c, not the 0x3ed718 -> 0x479a94 the card names.  The harness staging the card's cell made the original run `blx` into garbage (UC_ERR_INSN_INVALID at 0x1c5cb4); the pc-relative arithmetic (0x1c5ca4 + 0x00227a78) is the authority, and binding() now re-derives all five slots from the pool words.

CARD DRIFT: the F3 message string is at 0x350864 and reads "Attempting to add instance %d multiple times to a layer", not " ERROR: Adding too many variables" at 0x35285c.  Everything else matched case for case; this was the single identity diff left before the string was corrected.

the 0x1c5abc/0x1c5ac0 probe early-out (`tst r2,r4 ; bpl`) can only fall through when the table mask carries bit 31, i.e. for a 0x80000000-entry table: with any sane mask the probe ALWAYS advances and the ordering decision is made at 0x1c5c24 (`cmp r7,r5 ; blt`).  Case F3-w is the one that makes that comparison observable at all, because the probe only chooses new-vs-reuse: flipping the comparison is invisible unless the walk would have found our hash further on.

CRoom::AddInstance returns CollisionInsert's r0, not `inst`: 0x1ab734 seeds r0 and 0x1ab73c is a `b` after the frame is popped. With a void callee that is inst in practice, but the body gives no such guarantee and the differential proves the pass-through with a distinctive stub return (f1_returns_callee_r0).

F1 has NO duplicate check and does not look at +0x174: re-registering an instance that is already the chain head makes it point at ITSELF (case F1-i: inst->next == inst), bumps room+0x88 from 1 to 2, and appends a second id-hash node for the same key.  The idempotence the cards describe lives in F2/F3's +0x174 gate, not here -- so a second call on an already-registered instance is safe only because F2/F3 do nothing, while the chain and the count are already corrupted.

the chain sort key is the SNAPSHOT at +0x184 (case F1-f): a node whose live depth was changed after insertion still sorts by the value captured when it was inserted, and the empty-chain branch copies +0x180 into +0x184 with `ldr`/`str`, not through a float operation.
F2 raises the same r0-residue question on its four gate exits: the function is void and never writes r0, so each exit returns the first argument.  The translation reproduces it and says so.
F3's error path returns the vtable callee's r0 as well, and writes no field: an instance that already owns a live element is left exactly as it was (fail-soft, not an assert).

the 36 B pool grows by `capacity` elements and then DOUBLES the capacity unconditionally -- including on the capacity <= 0 path, which allocates nothing (case F3-k).  A pool with capacity 0 and a non-empty free list therefore still hands out an element and keeps capacity 0.

census_selftest.note: a mutation that leaves the gate green means the census does not actually bind the translation to the bytes
